title: European Countries Demand Russia’s Exclusion from Venice Architecture Biennale
summary: Ten countries in the European Union have urged the European Commission to keep Russia out of Venice’s 2027 architecture biennale. The effort is led by Poland and includes Austria, Croatia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Latvia, Lithuania, and Sweden. title: Scotland’s Paisley Museum to Reopen in Early 2027
summary: Paisley Museum, which holds one of the largest municipal art collections in Scotland, is set to reopen its doors to the public early next year following the first major renovation in its 150-year history. title: San Diego Announces New Contemporary Art Museum, The Strauss
summary: San Diego is getting a new contemporary art museum. The 12,000-square-foot space, called the Strauss Family Gallery, will open next spring. The museum will be free and open to the public. title: L.A Gallery The Landing Shutters After Fourteen Years
summary: The Landing, a much-loved Los Angeles gallery, has closed its doors, Artnews reports. The gallery operated in a 2,800-square-foot space on Jefferson Boulevard and represented a roster of both historical and living artists, including Jeremy Anderson, Yevgeniya Baras, Lenore Tawney, Ruth Asawa, and Brenda Goodman. title: The New Museum Announces Partnership With Vega Foundation
summary: The New Museum has announced a multiyear partnership with the Toronto-based Vega Foundation, an organization dedicated to commissioning and supporting video art. It was launched by Elisa Nuyten, a New Museum board member. The Vega foundation primarily provides opportunities to emerging and mid-career artists who work in film and video. summary: Art Basel Miami Beach is set to open on December 4, but the collective Artists 4 Artists Miami has launched a campaign to boycott the fair, inviting local artists, curators, gallerists, collectors, and residents to abstain from participating and to consider long-term alternatives to the commercial juggernaut. title: Contested Van Gogh Fetches Eye-Watering $190.4 Million at Auction
summary: Vincent van Gogh’s 1890 Châtaigniers en fleurs (Blossoming Chestnut Trees) sold for $190.4 million at Sotheby’s in New York last night, smashing the artist’s auction record and blowing past the $180 million it had been expected to command. title: Sydney Announces Basic Income Program For Artists
summary: The city of Sydney has launched its “artist living grants” program, where 40 artists are given $25,000, about $16,650 USD, no strings attached. The program is based on an income for artists grant that was introduced in Ireland three years ago. It was just made permanent this past winter, giving 2,000 creatives €325 a week. […]

title: Krist Gruijthuijsen Named Director of Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam
summary: The Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam has announced Krist Gruijthuijsen as its new director. Gruijthuijsen arrives to the institution from Finland’s EMMA – Espoo Museum of Modern Art, where he has served as director since 2025, and from Kunsthaus Zürich, where he is curator at large. title: Iraq Museum to Reopen After Two Years of Renovations
summary: The Iraq Museum in Baghdad will reopen December 1, as two years of major renovations are completed, according to Ali Al-Dakhili, Iraq’s minister of tourism and antiquities. The space features new galleries for the display of the museum’s extensive collection of antiquities. summary: Art Bridges Foundation has announced that it will give $9.5 million to extend its Access For All Initiative, which has helped 64 museums across the US to offer free admission and community-based programming. summary: The Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago has announced a gift of 65 works of art from Chicago collectors Sandra and Jack Guthman.
